headline: Dry and cool through Sunday afternoon around Glendale and Los Angeles, with light rain Sunday night into Monday and a smaller chance midweek before a dry, mild Thanksgiving, while forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding during Thanksgiving week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A weak disturbance passing this afternoon and evening brings only scattered light showers north of Point Conception, a few hundredths of an inch at most, while Glendale and the rest of Los Angeles County stay dry. Highs run around 5 degrees below normal. Tonight, weak northeast winds blow from the land in the usual wind-prone areas but stay below advisory levels, and it turns chilly, with some areas dropping below freezing.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday is dry, and the light winds from the land warm things a bit west of the mountains, with highs in the mid to upper 60s. Dry weather lasts through at least Sunday afternoon, then a weak system brings a decent chance of measurable rain Sunday night into Monday morning, totaling a quarter inch or less with no flooding issues expected. Highs change only slightly from day to day Sunday and Monday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The next system, Tuesday night through Wednesday night, doesn't look very impressive. Rain is likely in San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara Counties with 0.10 to 0.50 inch (more around Rocky Butte), while Los Angeles and Ventura Counties have lower chances and a tenth of an inch or less. Thanksgiving Day and Friday look dry as high pressure builds and weak winds from the land develop, with highs in the mid 60s to mid 70s.

coast: Forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding Thanksgiving week, from a combination of unusually high sea levels (warmer ocean water expanding), extra-high spring tides with the moon at its closest, and a large, long-period swell from the west. For the Central Coast, Ventura and Los Angeles County beaches, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 3 AM Monday to 3 AM Wednesday (shallow flooding of beach parking lots and low roads, moderate beach erosion), followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon, when the swell arrives and significant impacts seem probable. Peak high tides come between about 8:45 and 10 AM, around 8.2 to 8.6 feet in Los Angeles and Ventura Counties and 7.9 to 8.2 feet on the Central Coast, with a reasonable worst case 0.3 to 0.5 foot higher; if upgraded to a warning, expect more extensive flooding farther inland, a moderate to high risk of damaging flooding of coastal roads and buildings, and significant erosion. Areas of greatest concern include Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Long Beach/Naples in LA County, Faria to Silver Strand Beach and Ventura Harbor in Ventura County, and Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes and the Cayucos, Avila and Pismo piers on the Central Coast; for the Santa Barbara South Coast (Santa Barbara to Rincon, Jalama Beach) and the islands, a Coastal Flood Advisory runs 3 AM Monday to 3 PM Thursday. A High Surf Advisory and Beach Hazards Statement run until 3 PM Friday, elevated to high surf is likely through Thanksgiving week, and more coastal alerts will likely be needed for Friday the 27th; officials advise sandbagging flood-prone property and staying off rock jetties and flooded roads and walkways. Offshore, conditions are much improved but remain hazardous for small craft, with Small Craft Advisories ending at 9 PM Friday or 3 AM Saturday depending on the area, then fairly mild Saturday; a weak front Sunday into Monday should have little impact, while a stronger cold front Tuesday night into Wednesday brings the best chance of wind and rain off the Central Coast, possible small-craft-level northwest to west winds south of Point Conception Wednesday and Wednesday night, and large seas returning mid to late week.
watch_for: Below-freezing early mornings in some areas tonight and this weekend.
Light rain Sunday night into Monday morning (a quarter inch or less), and how much reaches Los Angeles County with Wednesday's system.
Whether the Wednesday–Thursday Coastal Flood Watch is upgraded to a warning as the large swell meets the highest morning tides (about 8:45–10 AM).
confidence: Forecasters say the models agree well for both the weekend and next week, giving good confidence in the light rain amounts and a dry Thanksgiving; the main uncertainty is exactly how the swell timing lines up with the peak tides, though significant coastal impacts seem probable either way.
